title: Insulin Pump Program Compliance Manual: Written Orders and Authorization Grants
content:
## Section 1 — The written order

Every shipment on an Insulin Pump Program rests on a written order from the treating prescriber that names the item, the billing units per 30 days, the order date and the prescriber's NPI. The order is valid for the tier's written-order validity in calendar months counted from its order date, the valid-through date being the day before the same calendar day that many months later (falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist), and Larkfield records that valid-through date when the order is received.

*Hypothetical example:* with a 12-month validity, an order signed on 10 June of one year is valid through 9 June of the following year.

## Section 2 — Tiers that require prior authorization

On tiers where prior authorization is required, Larkfield submits a prior authorization request to the payer once the written order is on file and moves the program from referral received to pending authorization. The payer's approval is recorded as an authorization grant on the basis of a payer prior authorization, carrying the payer's PA reference, the approved units and the approved span, which runs the tier's prior-authorization validity in calendar months from the decision date unless the payer's approval states an earlier valid-through date, in which case the payer's date governs.

## Section 3 — Tiers without prior authorization

On tiers where prior authorization is not required, Larkfield records the authorization grant itself on the basis of the written order (a written-order basis, or a self-pay-order basis on the self-pay tier), valid from the order date through the order's valid-through date, for the billing units the order covers within that span.

## Section 4 — Request priority and payer decision times

A prior authorization request is submitted as expedited only when the prescriber states on the order that waiting the standard decision time could seriously jeopardize the patient's life or health; otherwise it is standard. The payer is expected to decide within the tier's standard decision time in calendar days of a standard request, or within the tier's expedited decision time in hours of an expedited one.

## Section 5 — Renewal of a prior authorization

A renewal request for a prior authorization may be submitted no earlier than the tier's renewal lead time in calendar days before the valid-through date of the authorization it renews, counted backward in calendar days from that valid-through date with the earliest submission day itself allowed, and it requires a written order that is valid beyond that valid-through date.

| Hypothetical case (30-day lead time; authorization valid through day D) | Renewal may be submitted |
|---|---|
| Submitted 31 days before D | No — earlier than the lead time allows |
| Submitted exactly 30 days before D | Yes — the earliest submission day itself is allowed |
| Submitted 10 days before D, written order valid through D only | No — the order must be valid beyond D |
| Submitted 10 days before D, written order valid past D | Yes |

## Section 6 — Activation, denials and clinical documents

1. A program is activated only when an authorization grant on file for the program is valid on the activation date.
2. A payer denial of a prior authorization is recorded with the payer's denial reason; the program stays in pending authorization while the prescriber supplies further documentation or a new request is made, and it closes only under the program's administrative closure rules.
3. Clinical documents are recorded with the purpose they serve and the visit date they document, and a document serves only the purpose recorded on it.
